text: The repressilator, engineered by Elowitz and Leibler (2000), produces sustained oscillations in gene expression. Which network topology generates this behavior?
choices: Two mutually repressing genes that also each self-activate, producing a bistable toggle switch
A single gene that directly represses its own promoter (negative autoregulation)
A ring of three transcriptional repressors, each repressing the next, forming a delayed negative feedback loop
A coherent feed-forward loop with AND logic at the output gene
explanation: The repressilator connects three repressor genes in a cycle (each represses the next), a negative feedback loop with enough delay -- from the multiple steps around the ring -- to produce sustained oscillations, following the same general principle as the Goodwin oscillator. Choice 0 describes a bistable toggle switch (mutual repression), which is a switch, not an oscillator. Simple negative autoregulation (choice 1) reaches a stable steady state faster and does not oscillate on its own, and a coherent feed-forward loop (choice 3) produces a delay in activation, not sustained oscillation.
